title: Run the Lambda and CloudFront SSE feasibility spike
description:
Run Test 1 from docs/FEASIBILITY_TESTS.md as disposable spike code.

Acceptance criteria:
- Emit numbered SSE frames every 250 ms for at least 20 minutes.
- Capture client receive times for direct and CloudFront paths.
- Report p50, p95, batching, disconnect boundary, and Last-Event-ID recovery.
- Repeat with a backgrounded tab and mobile Safari.
- Record the pass or failure branch in the gated design document.

Not included: DynamoDB, authentication, model calls, workers, or production code.

comments.text:
# Implementation plan (manager)

This is the plan a Composer 2.5 implementer will follow. Spike only. Do not productionize.

## Purpose

Answer Test 1 in docs/FEASIBILITY_TESTS.md: can a Lambda function URL behind CloudFront hold SSE for a model-turn-shaped request and deliver 250ms chunks one at a time?

The entire cloud API is gated on this. Record numbers. Pick a front door from evidence. Then destroy or clearly isolate the spike so it cannot become the product.

## Non-negotiables

- Spike code is throwaway. Not in python/src. Not in quality gates (black/ruff/behave/pytest CI must not grow a dependency on this).
- Every AWS resource is CDK in infra/. No console creates. No aws lambda create-function by hand.
- The product stack is Python. The spike Lambda must be Python with Lambda Web Adapter (or a custom runtime). Do not use the Node streamifyResponse path just because it is easier. We need to know if OUR stack streams.
- No DynamoDB, auth, model, worker, or real tokens.
- No emojis. No "support both ways" product paths. Measuring two transports is the experiment, not a dual production design.
- Do not extend the in-memory RealtimeSubscription / TurnStream kernel.
- Scale-to-zero remains a requirement. Do not add an ALB or an always-on process "to make the spike easier."
- Long, clear names. Sphinx docstrings on any public Python the spike exposes.

## What to build

Directory: spikes/sse-transport/ plus a CDK stack infra/lib/sse-spike-stack.ts named something like ChatticusSseSpike so it is obviously not the product control plane.

1. Python Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter)
   - RESPONSE_STREAM invoke mode on the function URL.
   - Content-Type: text/event-stream
   - Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store
   - Do not set Content-Encoding. Identity only.
   - Emit SSE frames every 250ms: event id (monotonic integer), data JSON {seq, server_unix_ms}.
   - Honor Last-Event-ID: resume seq at last_id+1, no gaps, no duplicates.
   - Timeout 900 seconds (Lambda max) so the 15-minute boundary is observed on the direct path.
   - Run at least 20 minutes of intended emit; when Lambda dies, that IS a result (document the wall clock of the last frame).
   - Query param or path to cap duration for short local checks (e.g. 30s) so we are not forced to wait 20 minutes on every deploy.

2. Function URL
   - Auth type NONE for the spike only. Document that production will not do this.
   - CORS open enough for the harness origin.

3. CloudFront
   - Origin: the function URL.
   - Cache policy: CachingDisabled.
   - Origin read timeout: 60s if quota forbids more; try 180s if the account allows it. Record which value deployed.
   - Viewer-request function (CloudFront Function or Function URL OAC-compatible equivalent): strip Accept-Encoding so CloudFront/Lambda cannot 502 on Content-Encoding mismatch.
   - Optional origin access control if it does not break streaming. If OAC plus POST/streaming is painful, public function URL for the spike is acceptable; record the choice.
   - Custom domain is not required.

4. Measurement harness
   - A static HTML+JS page using EventSource (not fetch) because that is the browser API production will use.
   - Two buttons or two URLs: direct function URL, CloudFront URL.
   - For each frame: seq, server_unix_ms, client_unix_ms, inter-frame gap, ttfb for the first frame.
   - Detect batching: multiple frames arriving in the same event-loop turn or with near-zero gaps after a long pause.
   - On error/close: record last seq, duration, error message.
   - Reconnect test: force close after N frames, reconnect with Last-Event-ID (EventSource does this if ids were sent), assert the next seq is last+1 with no skip.
   - Downloadable JSON summary: p50/p95/p99 inter-frame gap, count, duration, first-byte ms, reconnect result, whether the stream ended at a documented boundary.
   - Playwright (or equivalent) script for: foreground desktop, and one run with the page hidden/backgrounded if the environment can do it.
   - Mobile Safari: cannot be faked here. Ship a one-page checklist and the live URL. Do not invent Safari numbers.

## How to run

Document in spikes/sse-transport/README.md:

```
cd infra && npm install && npx cdk deploy ChatticusSseSpike
# open harness, run Playwright against outputs
```

Also document destroy: npx cdk destroy ChatticusSseSpike.

## Measurements required before calling the task done

Direct function URL:
- Warm run, >= several minutes (full 20 min at least once, or until Lambda 15 min kill, whichever comes first).
- p50, p95 inter-frame gap vs 250ms cadence (pass bar: p95 under ~400ms if frames arrive individually).
- TTFB.
- Observed disconnect boundary (expect ~15 min Lambda).
- Last-Event-ID reconnect without loss.

CloudFront path, same metrics:
- Expected disconnect near origin read timeout (30/60/180s), not 15 min. That is a pass if documented and reconnect works, not a fail.
- Compare buffering vs direct. If CloudFront batches to seconds, that is the CloudFront-buffers failure branch.
- TTFB (500-800ms has been reported; measure it against the 400ms p95 bar).

Failure branches (follow docs/FEASIBILITY_TESTS.md, do not invent a fourth architecture):
- CloudFront buffers: try function URL with custom domain, or HTTP API. Record which streams.
- Lambda streaming batchy on Python/LWA: try API Gateway streaming; then stop. Do not quietly add always-on.
- Nothing streams: write that Challenge 1 reopens. Do not "fix" it by violating requirement 7.

## Documentation to update when numbers exist

- Record the result in docs/DESIGN_CHALLENGES.md challenge 1 (the document this test gates): what streamed, what did not, chosen front door, measured gaps, disconnect boundaries.
- Delete Test 1 from docs/FEASIBILITY_TESTS.md only after the result is in DESIGN_CHALLENGES.md. That file holds open questions only.
- Do not write a new design document.

## Git

- Feature branch: cursor/sse-feasibility-spike-4a21 (lowercase).
- Do not commit .env, credentials, or captured PII.
- Do not add spike to python quality-gate paths.
- Commit message: describe the spike and that results go in DESIGN_CHALLENGES.

## Definition of done for the implementer

- CDK synth succeeds.
- Deploy succeeds in account 335163751677 region us-east-1 (credentials are present).
- At least direct and CloudFront automated measurements exist as committed JSON or markdown tables in spikes/sse-transport/results/ (no secrets).
- DESIGN_CHALLENGES.md updated with the result.
- Test 1 removed from FEASIBILITY_TESTS.md if and only if the result is recorded.
- README explains destroy.
- Mobile Safari listed as human-needed if not run, not as a fake pass.

If AWS deploy fails on permissions, stop and report. Do not work around with console clicks.
